item.title: research
item.content:encoded:
Given that the loop is fairly static, and emits light and energy bursts, there is a potential avenue of analysis that I have not seen suggested so far. With the Foundations access to advanced supercomputers, and advanced programmers and novel analysis programs and sensors, it is not inconceivable that a set of full window photon sensors could be constructed. With the right configuration and sensitivity, one can track the backscatter (subsurface scatter?) of all light sources with in the room. With enough data and analysis, the scene can be recreated digitally, slowly resolving the objects hidden from direct line of sight. This would also eventually let the screens and writing be resolved. Several of the algorithms and processes needed to do this already exist in the creation of digital media like movies and video games. It is simply more complicated to do it in reverse.

Thermal analysis, and analysis of naturally occurring x-ray and radiographic signatures, may also reveal more details beneath the cleansuits. If the scene also emits the naturally present neutrinos of the event, even more information may be gathered. Granted, currently neutrino detection tech is hideously bulky and expensive, but the Foundation has some pretty good tech hidden away. Especially with 914 to help refine things.

item.title: Hmm
item.content:encoded:
First, let me just say that this is magnificent. Great work, Raven.

Second…

if light can get out… can light get in?

Can we measure stuff in there by bouncing lasers off it?

I assume we've done spectrographic analysis of the machine's Burst Of Light… most forms of radiation involve particle emission… particles have mass — mass that's negligible at the macroscopic level, but still mass…

hmm.

I'm thinking of time and space being equivalent.

I'm thinking about why it's so impossible to get things into that room… about resistance, about potential energy… about gravity wells…

I'm thinking about event horizons… and being on the wrong side of one. Light can emerge from there… can it go back in?

Consider, again, the particles emitted… and think about Hawking radiation.

Could this time loop be - very, very slowly, AGONIZINGLY slowly - evaporating?
